name: Bilirubin Encephalopathy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Laboratory Diagnostic Criteria for Kernicterus

criteria.description: Serum unconjugated bilirubin levels significantly elevated above age-specific thresholds
Presence of characteristic neurological signs including lethargy, hypotonia progressing to hypertonia, and opisthotonus
MRI findings showing bilateral basal ganglia and brainstem abnormalities consistent with bilirubin toxicity
Abnormal auditory brainstem response indicating auditory pathway involvement

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Elevated unconjugated bilirubin levels plus characteristic neurological signs; supportive imaging or auditory testing may aid confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical supported by laboratory and imaging findings; early recognition is critical to prevent permanent damage

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic movement disorder seen in chronic kernicterus
searchTerms: movement disorder with mixed chorea and athetosis

pathognomonic.notes: Sensorineural hearing loss due to auditory pathway damage
Severe hyperextension of the neck and back in acute phase

common.notes: Initial decreased muscle tone before progression

occasional.notes: Increased muscle tone developing after hypotonia
Respiratory irregularities due to brainstem involvement
Dysregulation due to central nervous system involvement

rare.notes: Due to brainstem and basal ganglia damage
Severe motor dysfunction in chronic phase

searchTerms: hearing impairment not due to nerve

laboratory: Normal or mildly elevated liver function tests
imaging: MRI showing bilateral T2 hyperintensity in globus pallidus and subthalamic nuclei
genetic: No specific genetic mutations; risk increased with G6PD deficiency or other hemolytic disorders
other: Clinical history of severe neonatal jaundice

distinguishingFeatures: Diffuse brain injury pattern on MRI

redFlags: Rapidly rising serum bilirubin levels above critical thresholds
Onset of neurological symptoms in neonate with jaundice
Failure to respond to phototherapy or exchange transfusion
references: American Academy of Pediatrics Subcommittee on Hyperbilirubinemia. Management of hyperbilirubinemia in the newborn infant 35 or more weeks of gestation. Pediatrics. 2004;114(1):297-316.
Shapiro SM. Bilirubin toxicity in the developing nervous system. Pediatr Neurol. 2003;29(5):410-421.
Watchko JF. Kernicterus and bilirubin-induced neurologic dysfunction (BIND) - a spectrum of neonatal neurotoxicity. Semin Fetal Neonatal Med. 2006;11(6): 423-429.
